paragraph: [Lei 22/11 of 17 June 2011 created the Agência de Protecção de Dados](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2011/lei-n-o-22-11-de-17-de-junho/>). [Decreto Presidencial 277/19 of 6 September 2019 appointed a president and two executive administrators](<https://lex.ao/docs/presidente-da-republica/2019/decreto-presidencial-n-o-277-19-de-06-de-setembro/>). In the last twelve months it [fined Lizíria, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 on 10 August 2026](<https://sapo.pt/artigo/agencia-de-proteccao-de-dados-de-angola-multa-hotel-diamante-em-115-mil-dolares-6a857707bf642b2fcc16d93b>). On 14 July 2026 it [fined the Luanda water utility EPAL USD 150,000 over customer data](<https://www.expansao.co.ao/empresas/detalhe/agencia-de-proteccao-de-dados-ja-aplicou-multas-de-25-milhoes-usd-desde-2022-73575.html>). Its [own register lists 15 fines for 2022 to 2026](<https://apd.ao/ao/gca/index.php?id=218&preview=1>), and [PTI counts three of them in 2025](<https://pti.ao/apd-ja-aplicou-mais-de-1-milhao-de-dolares-em-multas-este-ano/>). No count published by the authority itself has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

The [law adopted on 15 January 2026 creates an independent administrative authority responsible for enforcing data protection](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burundi-lawmakers-approve-data-protection-framework-as-digitalisation-accelerates>), and the [law was promulgated on 10 March 2026](<https://communityvoice.bi/1489-2/>). In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026, the Council of Ministers [approved a draft decree on the agency's duties, membership and resources](<https://www.burunditimes.com/burundi-faces-data-protection-test-as-eac-advances-regional-rules/>), subject to adjustments. No appointment to the agency has been found. No ruling against an organisation and no published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

[Book V of the Digital Code, Articles 462 to 473, established the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/loi-2017-20/download>) as an independent administrative authority. In the last twelve months, [Decree 2026-422 of 1 July 2026 named its eight members](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/decret-2026-422/download>), who [were sworn in before the Supreme Court on 6 November 2026](<https://www.24haubenin.info/?Les-nouveaux-membres-de-l-APDP-pretent-serment=>). Its [2025 report gives 907 files examined, 64 inspection missions, 20 complaints treated and 75 compliance certificates issued](<https://www.lanation.bj/numerique/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-en-2025-au-benin-lapdp-dresse-un-bilan-sous-le-signe-de-la-conformite>). No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

The 2021 data protection law creates the Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) as the supervisory authority. It has [nine members appointed by decree](<https://www.fonction-publique.gov.bf/fileadmin/user_upload/storage/22-08-2021-C2-LOI-N__001-2021_AN_portant_protection_des_personnes.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 3 August 2026 the legislative assembly [adopted a bill](<https://www.aib.media/burkina-les-deputes-adoptent-la-loi-portant-creation-de-larcod-issue-de-la-fusion-du-csc-et-de-la-cil/>) merging the CIL into a new regulator, ARCOD. [A decree of 16 October 2026 named W. Louis Modeste Ouédraogo president of the merged regulator](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article150089>). [On 19 November 2026 the Council of Ministers named the ten councillors of ARCOD's first college](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article150924=>). No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

Botswana's Information and Data Protection Commission works under the Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024. The Minister said it was [established in 2022](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/87795>). Mmegi reported on 11 February 2026 that [Kepaletswe Somolekae is the newly appointed commissioner](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/new-data-commission-tightens-compliance-oversight/news>). In the last twelve months, in a [public notice dated 17 July 2026](<https://na.co.bw/data-commission-orders-suspension-of-dpsm-epayslip-portal-over-privacy-law-breaches/>) the commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM. [DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026](<https://www.mmegi.bw/news/govt-e-payslip-fails-data-protection-compliance-test/news>). No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

Article 57 of Loi n° 24.001, promulgated in January 2024, gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy [twelve months from promulgation to set up the data protection agency](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Loi_24_001_portant_protection_des_donnes_a_caractere__personnel.pdf>). Data Protection Africa states that the [authority has not yet been appointed, as of 28 January 2026](<https://dataprotection.africa/central-african-republic>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

[Law No. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013](<https://anssi.gouv.ci/documents/14/Loi_2013-450_19_juin_2013_relative_%C3%A0_la_protection_des_donn%C3%A9es_%C3%A0_caract%C3%A8re_personnel.pdf>) governs personal data protection. A [decree of 4 February 2015](<https://www.artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/decret_2015_79.pdf>) names ARTCI as the body that imposes withdrawals and fines under it. On 16 January 2024 the authority [issued decision 2024-0996, a warning and formal notice to METFPA and Kaydan Groupe](<https://www.autoritedeprotection.ci/decisions/>). In the last twelve months, in July 2026 Agence Ecofin [reported 210 complaints and 18 inspections, and no financial sanction by ARTCI](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0707-139967-cote-divoire-ce-que-certinum-va-changer-pour-les-entreprises-et-les-administrations>). No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent period has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

[Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024](<https://prc.cm/fr/multimedia/documents/10258-loi-n-2024-017-du-23-12-2024-web>) sets up the Autorité as an independent public body in charge of data protection. The law names no head or members. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the OBS-CC observatory said [it was still not installed, and the decree to put it in place had not been taken](<https://obs-cc.org/suivi-recommandations-fncc/>). No source says the Authority's head or members have been appointed. No ruling and no published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

Article 262 of the [Digital Code of 13 March 2023](<https://are.gouv.cd/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/04042023-ORDONNANCE-LOI-23-010-DU-13-MARS-PORTANT-CODE-DU-NUMERIQUE_compressed.pdf>) creates an independent Autorité de protection des données. A [ministerial order of 17 August 2024](<https://droitnumerique.cd/autorite-de-protection-des-donnees/>) gave its missions to the telecoms regulator ARPTC until it is set up. In the last twelve months, on 13 September 2026, [Beto.cd reported](<https://beto.cd/onip-rgph2-deux-comptages-population-autorite-protection-donnees/>) that the authority is not installed. The ARPTC's [decision of September 2025, published on 23 April 2026](<https://www.africadataprotection.org/rdc-publication-au-journal-officiel-de-la-decision-fixant-la-procedure-des-formalites-prealables.html>), sets the authorisations and declarations owed to it. No ruling against an organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

Congo's National Personal Data Protection Commission has members appointed under [Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/01/22/congo-launches-commission-to-strengthen-personal-data-protection-and-digital-governance/>). In the last twelve months, on 22 January 2026 the ICT minister [installed the members](<https://itweb.africa/article/congo-brazzaville-intros-data-protection-commission/>) and described the commission as able to advise, warn and sanction. That states a power, not its use. No ruling against an organisation has been found, nor any complaint count or annual report. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

The 2014 data protection law [institutes a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés](<https://anaden.org/uploads/media/63076edf43d1e/loi-portant-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-de-lunion-des-comores.pdf>) in Article 19, with nine members to be named by decree under Article 24. A 2025 review states that, as of 2024, the authority was [not yet constituted or operational](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-the-comoros-data-protection-law>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No appointment, ruling or published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

Cape Verde's National Data Protection Commission (CNPD) [marked its tenth anniversary in March 2025](<https://expressodasilhas.cv/pais/2025/03/19/presidente-da-cnpd-defende-dialogo-entre-os-ecossistemas-de-governanca-de-dados-para-equilibrar-regulacao-da-ia/96153>) under its president, Faustino Varela. The Assembly's budget [appropriates CVE 36,313,115 for 2025](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/4674538/Lei%20que%20aprova%20o%20OE%202025.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 23 February 2026 its head signed a [joint statement with 60 other authorities](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>). The same budget source says the CNPD [published no activity report for any year since 2016](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/4674538/Lei%20que%20aprova%20o%20OE%202025.pdf>). No ruling against an organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

The National Assembly voted Djibouti's Digital Code on 30 June 2025, and [Jones Day reports that the regime establishes the CNDP](<https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2025/07/national-assembly-of-the-republic-of-djibouti-approves-digital-code>), the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data. A [review of 5 November 2025](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-djiboutis-data-protection-law>) describes it as independent with administrative and financial autonomy, and does not say it has been constituted or its members appointed. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling by the commission and no published figures have been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

Algeria's national data protection authority (ANPDP) enforces Law 18-07, and in July 2026 [Samir Bourehil is named as its president](<https://www.elmoudjahid.dz/fr/actualite/securisation-de-l-espace-numerique-l-engagement-sans-faille-de-la-dgsn-255551>). In the last twelve months it [adopted a deliberation at its sitting of 15 July 2026](<https://anpdp.dz/ar/storage/2026/07/MOD-19-07-2026-v2.pdf>), and on 11 November 2026 it announced [Deliberation No. 05 on personal data in CVs](<https://www.lesoirdalgerie.com/actualites/l-anpdp-encadre-le-traitement-des-informations-contenues-dans-les-cv-160122>). It also [issued a decision in early 2026 on employee and candidate drug test results](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>). No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

[Law 151 of 2020 created the Personal Data Protection Center](<https://www.actpol.org/research/egypt-data-protection-deadline-north-africa>) (PDPC), and the executive regulations of November 2025 [confirm it as the supervisory authority](<https://accesspartnership.com/opinion/egypt-finalises-executive-regulations-to-the-personal-data-protection-law-pdpl>). An [acting chief executive, Susan El-Okbawy, leads it](<https://gate.ahram.org.eg/Massai/News/5884624.aspx>), and ACTPOL states it had [no board as of January 2026](<https://www.actpol.org/research/egypt-data-protection-deadline-north-africa>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026 it [launched its electronic portal](<https://www.bakermckenzie.com/en/insight/publications/2026/10/egypt-personal-data-protection-law-update>) for accreditation, licence and permit applications. The centre had published no decisions on its website when ACTPOL checked on 25 September 2026. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

[Law Lab Africa](<https://research.lawlab.africa/eritrea/>) states that no supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. [Levellers](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-eritrea>) states that Eritrea has no data protection statute and has not appointed an authority, on a page reviewed on 8 June 2026. The [Horn of Africa Initiative](<https://hoainitiative.org/sites/default/files/2025-09/25th%20HoAI%20Ministerial%20-%20Background%20Paper%20on%20Digital%20Integration%20Update.pdf>) update of June 2025 says Eritrea remains without regulatory oversight for data protection. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

The data protection proclamation [designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulator](<https://www.aln.africa/ethiopia-new-data-protection-law>), in an overview of July 2024. By November 2025 [Shega](<https://shega.co/news/one-year-on-ethiopia-s-personal-data-protection-law-faces-a-slow-path-to-enforcement>) described the Authority as enforcing the law, and its Director General, Balcha Reba, said data processors and collectors now need its permission. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling against a named organisation has been found, and no published count of decisions or complaints. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

[Article 7 of Loi n°025/2023](<https://www.apdpvp.ga/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Gabon-Loi-025-2023-du-12-juillet-2023-portant-modification-de-la-loi-001-2011-du-25-septembre-relative-a-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel.pdf>) creates the APDPVP as an independent administrative authority. By [deliberation n°073 of 25 April 2024](<https://www.apdpvp.ga/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/SANCTION-CITIBANK-25-AVRIL-2024.pdf>) its plenary fined Citibank Gabon S.A. 90,000,000 FCFA. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 its president [demanded the immediate suspension of a data-sharing operation](<https://www.actpol.org/research/central-africa-laws-before-regulators-cameroon>), and on 4 September 2026 Joël Dominique Ledaga was still [speaking as head of the authority](<https://union.sonapresse.com/fr/joel-dominique-ledaga-pour-echanger-directement-avec-meta-tiktok-ou-instagram-il-faut-une-reponse>). No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

The [Data Protection Commission](<https://dataprotection.org.gh/data-protection-commission-acquires-new-vehicles-to-expand-regional-and-enforcement-operations/>) describes itself as an independent statutory body established under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843). In the last twelve months, on 14 October 2026 it [directed named companies to report to the police and regularise their registration](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/10/dpc-flags-six-companies-for-data-protection-breaches/>). They included Polytex Ghana Limited, JA Biney Packaging and Menkish Impex Ltd. On 13 October 2026 it [said it had registered 2,575 data controllers](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/10/dpc-strengthens-enforcement-after-registering-2575-data-controllers/>) in 2026. No published count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

The 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law [defines an Autorité de Protection and gives it functions](<https://assembleeguinee.org/loi-ndeg-l-2016-relative-la-cybersecurite-et-la-protection-des-donnees-caractere-personnel-en>) covering declarations, authorisations, transfer approval and investigation. It names no constituted body or members. In June 2024 the National Transition Council's commissions [debated a bill to establish the authority](<https://cnt.gov.gn/apdp/>), with the designation of members still contested. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

The [Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 (Act No. 11 of 2025, assented 7 November 2025)](<https://media2.mofo.com/v3/assets/blt5775cc69c999c255/blt7a10e6071e9d3fad/69d554b553df724b615c685d/personal-data-protection-and-privacy-act-2025.pdf>) names the Information Commission as the Commission. A [review of 26 December 2025](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-gambias-personal-data-protection-and-privacy-act-2025>) describes it as an independent oversight Commission. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 a [notice](<https://gambia.unfpa.org/en/vacancies/development-communication-strategy-information-commission-gambia>) has it developing a communication strategy on the Act. No ruling or published figure from the Commission has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

A speaker said on [22 September 2026](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-inter-la-cour-de-justice-de-la-cedeao-dispose-dun-cadre-pour-statuer-sur-les-droits-numeriques-selon-un-universitaire/>) that Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority, and that several institutions handle these matters sector by sector. The [Data Protection Africa factsheet](<https://dataprotection.africa/guinea-bissau/>), published 25 May 2022, states that the country has no data protection law and that its authority is not appointed. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

Articles 15 and 29 of [Law No. 1/2016](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Guinee-equatoriale-ley-1-2.016-de-proteccion-de-datos.pdf>), dated 22 July 2016, name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body. It is to be created by a decree that will fix its structure. [Data Protection Africa](<https://dataprotection.africa/equatorial-guinea/>), in a factsheet published 23 May 2022, states that the authority is not yet appointed or operational. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source says whether its head or members have been appointed since 2022. No ruling or figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was set up under the Data Protection Act, 2019. [Immaculate Kassait has been the first commissioner since 2020](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/09/30/kenya-data-protection-commissioner-shortlist/>). Its [own bulletin](<https://www.odpc.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ODPC-Data-Bulletin-12th-Edition.pdf>) gives running totals to March 2025, with 7,128 complaints received and 215 determinations. In the last twelve months, on 4 December 2025 it [ordered Platinum Credit to pay a complainant KES 400,000](<https://capitalfm.africa/odpc-platinum-credit-fined-400k-unlawful-data-use/>). In November 2026 Kassait said that over six years [the office handled more than 13,000 complaints and issued 459 determinations](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/11/15/odpc-compensation-powers/>). [President Ruto nominated Lydia Sitienei](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/11/10/kenya-nominates-lydia-sitienei-second-data-commissioner/>) to succeed her. No edition of the bulletin after March 2025 has been found.

Liberia's [Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024 was printed on 23 March 2026](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/An_Act_For_The_Collection_Processing_-Transmission_-Storage_-Protection_-And_Use_Of_Personal-_Information_In_Liberia_Printed_Version_20260323_063904.pdf>). Sections 8 and 10 give data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner. The Freedom of Information Act of 2010 created that body. In February 2025 a minister told the [Africa-China Reporting Project](<https://africachinareporting.com/liberia-struggles-to-enforce-privacy-and-data-protection-laws/>) that Liberia had no national data protection authority. In the last twelve months, the Act was printed on 23 March 2026. Nothing found says the Commissioner has begun acting under it, or that any ruling or figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

[SMEX said on 22 July 2026 that Libya currently has no functioning data protection authority](<https://smex.org/libyas-new-ai-strategy-celebrates-participation-yet-was-built-without-it/>), in its review of the country's new artificial intelligence strategy. The statement describes the position at that date, so no authority can be counted as appointed and in office. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found names a body that was ever set up, and no ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

As at 31 October 2025 the law firm [Z. Mayet and Associates](<https://zmayetlaw.co.ls/lesothos-outdated-data-protection-act-no-commissioner-no-teeth-what-should-change-next/>) states that the Commission and Commissioner mandated by the Data Protection Act had not been appointed. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 [Cenfri](<https://cenfri.org/articles/african-data-governance-reform-in-an-era-of-reform/>) said the Commission has remained unappointed, and [Digital Rights Alliance Africa](<https://digitalrightsalliance.africa/exploring-the-data-protection-and-data-governance-challenges-and-opportunities-in-lesotho/>) wrote that it had still not been established. Nothing found says the Commission or its Commissioner has since been appointed. No ruling or published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

Morocco's [CNDP](<https://www.cndp.ma/la-cndp-publie-de-nouvelles-deliberations/>), the national commission for the control of personal data protection, works under Law 09-08 and was [installed in 2010](<https://www.cndp.ma/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/CNDP-Communiqu_2_Publication_du_Registre_National_FR_-20230111.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 28 November 2025 it [validated five new deliberations](<https://www.cndp.ma/la-cndp-publie-de-nouvelles-deliberations/>), D-939 to D-943 of 2025. On 8 February 2026 it signed a [cooperation memorandum with Portugal's authority](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>), and in August 2026 it [informed parties and citizens of the data rules](<https://maroc.ma/fr/actualites/elections-legislatives-la-cndp-fixe-les-imperatifs-respecter-dans-le-traitement-des-donnees-caractere>) for the 23 September 2026 elections. No ruling against a named organisation is on record. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

Law 2014-038 provides for the CMIL: [article 28 institutes an independent authority](<https://www.assemblee-nationale.mg/media/archives_textes/pl/2014-038/Loi-n2014-038-sur-la-protection-des-donn%C3%A9es-%C3%A0-Kre-personnel.pdf>) of nine members with regulatory and sanctioning powers. Seven members were [sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025](<https://assemblee-nationale.mg/article/prestation-de-serment-des-membres-de-la-commission-malagasy-de-linformatique-et-des-libertes-cmil/>). In the last twelve months, a government announcement of 27 March 2026 says the [CMIL is now effectively in place](<https://digital.gov.mg/en/2026/03/27/rapport-annuel-sur-la-confidentialiteet-la-protection-des-donnees-a-madagascar/>), and its annual report, published January 2026, says [no processing declaration has been registered](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/11XR_I-6z6Y28qnrEjHABu3SOIbjWy6yW/view>). No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

Mali's [APDP](<https://primature.ml/apdp-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>) is an independent administrative authority of 15 members under Article 20 of Law 2013-015. Its 2025 annual report, [summarised by Sahel Tribune](<https://saheltribune.com/donnees-personnelles-lalerte-du-regulateur-malien/>), gives about 1,000 formal notices, fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints, 28 of them handled. The authority [fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA](<https://fr.apanews.net/community/mali-lapdp-examine-2-000-dossiers-et-un-projet-darrete/>) for obstructing a verification mission. In the last twelve months, it opened a [Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025](<https://lessor.ml/posts/autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-la-region-de-segou-a-son-antenne-6932a107b56bd>). It held its [second ordinary session on 3 August 2026](<https://orbiteinfo.com/mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1-000-dossiers-au-programme/>) with all commissioners present.

A [UNECA inception report of June 2025](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/sites/default/files/resources/documents/TICID/data-governance-framework-mozambique/en_project_inception_report_mozambique_data_governance_framework.pdf>) states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority. The [World Bank restructuring paper](<https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099012626175535228>) says the Data Protection Office was not yet established as of October 2025. A [September 2025 review](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-mozambiques-proposed-personal-data-protection-law>) says the draft law would give the role to the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

[Article 64 of Law 2017-020](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/112890/MRT-112890.pdf>) creates an independent Authority for Personal Data Protection attached to the Prime Minister. On 30 July 2025 it [adopted deliberation 005/2025](<https://www.apd.mr/%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%af%d8%a7%d9%88%d9%84%d8%a9-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-005-2025-%d8%aa%d8%aa%d8%b9%d9%84%d9%91%d9%82-%d8%a8%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%b4%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b7-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%af%d9%86%d9%8a%d8%a7-%d8%a7/>), a general rule and not a finding against an organisation. In the last twelve months, it held [monthly meetings on 29 April 2026](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-16/>) and [30 June 2026](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-18/>), and its president was [sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026](<https://rimweb.net/2026/10/08/le-president-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-prete-serment-pour-un-second-mandat/>). No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

The [Data Protection Office](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/AnnualReports/265-26-DPO%20AR%202024-SOFT%20COPY.pdf>) has operated since 16 February 2009 and enforces the Data Protection Act 2017. For [January to December 2024](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/AnnualReports/265-26-DPO%20AR%202024-SOFT%20COPY.pdf>) it reports 179 new complaints, 39 complaints closed, 105 personal data breaches notified and 112 cross-border transfers authorised. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 [regulations on data protection officers](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/117_The-Data-Protection_Designation-Tasks-and-Position-of-Data-Protection-Officers_Reg.pdf>) gave the Office roles in receiving notifications, certifying officers and approving training institutions. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

[Section 4 of the Data Protection Act, 2024](<https://cyrilla.org/api/files/1714974153599cf41tfelimj.pdf>) designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) as the Data Protection Authority. [The Act came into force on 3 June 2024](<https://itlawco.com/focus-areas/data-protection-and-privacy/malawis-data-protection-act-2024-an-overview/>). In the last twelve months, in July 2026 [Daniel Chiwoni was named as its Head of Data Protection](<https://www.nyasatimes.com/macra-consults-stakeholders-on-proposed-data-protection-registration-fees/>). On 11 November 2026 it [held a validation workshop on proposed registration fees in Blantyre](<https://www.dpa.mw/dpa-reviews-proposed-data-protection-registration-fees/>). No ruling against a named organisation has been found, and no published figures. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

A governance professional [wrote in The Namibian on 17 May 2026](<https://www.namibian.com.na/namibian-boards-need-to-rethink-data-privacy/>) that Namibia has no dedicated data protection authority and no comprehensive data protection law in force. A draft Data Protection Bill would create a supervisory authority, two analysts [wrote in Technews in April 2025](<https://technews.com.na/2025/04/29/is-namibias-data-protection-bill-good-or-bad/>), and the [2020 draft bill](<https://dataprotection.africa/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Namibia_DPA-Bill.pdf>) names it the Data Protection Supervisory Authority of Namibia. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

[Article 6 of Law 2022-59, as amended by Law 2023-31](<https://www.hapdp.ne/uploads/files/Loi-2022-59-consolidee.pdf>), created the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (HAPDP). [Its president took office on 18 September 2024](<https://www.lesahel.org/entretien-avec-le-president-de-la-haute-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-hapdp/>). In the last twelve months, [a presidential decree of 8 June 2026 abolished the HAPDP and ended its officials' functions](<https://anp.ne/niger-plusieurs-services-rattaches-ou-sous-tutelle-de-la-presidence-de-la-primature-et-du-secretariat-general-du-gouvernement-supprimes/>). Its missions passed to the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior. [An ordonnance of the same day repealed the provisions of the 2022 law that founded it](<https://www.africadataprotection.org/niger-suppression-de-la-haute-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel.html>). Nothing found says those ministries supervise data protection. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

The [2023 Data Protection Act created a formal Data Protection Commission](<https://www.dataphyte.com/topic/technology/who-protects-nigerias-digital-citizens/>), headed by National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji. On 18 February 2025 it [issued a Final Order fining Meta $32.8 million](<https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/headlines/832580-32-8-million-fine-dispute-meta-settles-with-nigerian-govt-out-of-court.html>). In 2025 it [fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500](<https://www.rapdp.org/index.php/en/node/222>). In the last twelve months, it [issued a Notice of Investigation on 1 April 2026](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/04/07/ndpc-investigates-remita-and-sterling-bank-over-alleged-data-breach/>). In October 2026 Olatunji said it had [investigated more than 240 breach cases and issued over 20 major remediation orders](<https://thenigerialawyer.com/rogue-actors-are-exploiting-data-to-threaten-governance-nji-administrator-justice-adejumo-calls-for-stronger-judicial-capacity/>), giving no period. No count for a stated recent period has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the [supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>), an article of 26 January 2026 states. In December 2024 the East African Community said Rwanda is among [five of its eight Partner States that had established dedicated data protection authorities](<https://tanzaniatimes.net/south-sudan-fails-to-endorse-national-data-protection-law/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or fine against a named organisation has been found in the last three years. No count of complaints or decisions has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

No stage is set. A factsheet last updated on 24 May 2022 says Sudan has [no data protection authority appointed](<https://dataprotection.africa/sudan/>). No law found names an authority, and no source from the last three years says whether that still holds. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country has no data protection authority, and no law in force that names one.

[Law no. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008 set up the Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP)](<https://aps.sn/plus-de-300-dossiers-traites-par-la-commission-de-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-au-premier-trimestre-2026-officiel/>) as an independent administrative authority. In April 2024 its plenary [served a formal notice on SOLID SA](<https://senego.com/la-plateforme-kay-voter-mise-en-demeure-par-la-cdp-pour-des-sms-non-sollicites-sur-le-report-de-lelection_1688747.html>), operator of the Kay Voter platform. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 it [ordered a company to uninstall a meeting-room camera](<https://aps.sn/plus-de-300-dossiers-traites-par-la-commission-de-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-au-premier-trimestre-2026-officiel/>). It handled [317 files in January to March 2026](<https://aps.sn/plus-de-300-dossiers-traites-par-la-commission-de-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-au-premier-trimestre-2026-officiel/>) and [195 in April to June 2026](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Societe/donnees-personnelles-plus-de-190-dossiers-traites-par-la-cdp-entre-avril-et-juin_n_503047.html>). On 5 November 2026 it [warned the public about scams using AI voice cloning](<https://cdp.sn/actualites/52517c7a-0431-45a3-b40b-48f28bc2e965>).

No stage is set. No law found names a data protection authority in Sierra Leone, and no source from the last three years says the country has none. An authority is named only in a bill of 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country has no data protection authority, and no law in force that names one.

[Article 6 of the Data Protection Act establishes the Data Protection Authority as an independent agency](<https://moct.gov.so/en/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Somalia-Data-Protection-Act-2.pdf>), and it was [inaugurated on 24 February 2024](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/en/2024/02/26/somalia-inauguration-of-the-data-protection-authority>). In the last twelve months, by June 2026 it was [accepting registration applications from controllers and processors](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/02/somalia-data-protection-authority-enforces-nationwide-data-compliance-rules/>). Its [Registration Guidelines, version 1.0 of January 2026](<https://dpa.gov.so/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Registration-Guidelines.pdf>), set fees, a 30-day approval timeline and mandatory registration. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

A [2022 factsheet](<https://dataprotection.africa/south-sudan/>) stated that South Sudan had appointed no data protection authority and that no law established one. In December 2024 the [Tanzania Times](<https://tanzaniatimes.net/south-sudan-fails-to-endorse-national-data-protection-law/>) reported the East African Community as saying South Sudan was yet to form one. In February 2026 [Digital Rights Frontlines](<https://www.digitalrights.ngo/post/an-independent-data-protection-act-a-critical-part-to-south-sudan-s-digital-future>) said the country still lacks a fully operational, independent authority. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

São Tomé and Príncipe has a National Personal Data Protection Agency, the ANPDP, which the [2022 ALT Advisory factsheet](<https://dataprotection.africa/sao-tome-and-principe/>) says Law 03/2016 establishes, with an appointed head. In the last twelve months, on 1 June 2026 [Macau's data protection office](<https://www.gov.mo/pt/noticias/831008/>) signed a cooperation memorandum with it. In 2026 [Téla Nón](<https://www.telanon.info/politica/2026/04/15/52530/recenseamento-eleitoral-automatico-vai-ser-fiscalizado-pela-agencia-nacional-de-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais/>) described it as the body that by law authorises and supervises all data processing. A [2024 International Bar Association chapter](<https://www.ibanet.org/document?id=Digital-Regulations-in-the-Metaverse-Era-Sao-Tome-Principe>) says the agency imposes fines, but names no sanction, decision or count. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

The Data Protection Act 2022 designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority, as an [authority notice](<https://edpa.org.sz/assets/documents/notice%204.pdf>) states. Its [enforcement page](<https://www.edpa.org.sz/enforcement.html>) lists enforcement notices issued in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited. It lists one issued in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park. In the last twelve months, in early 2026 it [issued a directive](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>) requiring controllers and processors to map their data by 31 March 2026. In [September 2026](<https://eswatinipositivenews.online/edpa-takes-data-protection-services-closer-to-emaswati/>) it ran an outreach campaign. No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

Section 5 of the [Data Protection Act, 2023](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2023-12/Act%2024%20-%202023%20-%20Data%20Protection%20Act%202023.pdf>) names the Information Commission as the authority, and the Commission says it [took on the mandate at the end of December 2023](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/ATIA-Updated-Whitepaper-10.11.2025.pdf>). Its [2025 annual report](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/Annual-Report-2025.pdf>) shows a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a chief executive in post. In the last twelve months, the National Assembly [lists the 2025 report as published on 13 April 2026](<https://www.nationalassembly.sc/publications/reports/information-commission-seychelles-annual-report-2025>). No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

[Decree 2011/PR/2026 of 1 June 2026 appointed a director, replacing a predecessor, and a deputy director of the Direction du contrôle et de la protection des données personnelles](<https://www.alwihdainfo.com/tchad-nomination/>). The directorate is part of the Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Electronique (ANSICE). In the last twelve months, that decree filled its two senior posts. A July 2026 legal analysis states that [Loi n°007/PR/2015 gives ANSICE the formalities for data transfers](<https://thomasd-avocats.com/transfert-international-rapport-enquete-tchad-rgpd/>). No ruling, fine or order against a named organisation has been found. No count of decisions or complaints has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

Article 55 of the [2019 data protection law](<https://jo.gouv.tg/sites/default/files/JO/JOS_29_10_2019-64E%20ANNEE-N%C2%B026%20TER.pdf>) creates a national authority, the IPDCP, which [became operational in 2024](<https://levisionnaire.tg/protection-des-donnees-lipdcp-appelle-les-administrations-togolaises-a-accelerer-leur-mise-en-conformite/>) and [launched its activities on 28 March 2025](<https://www.togofirst.com/fr/tic/2903-16040-numerique-l-instance-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-demarre-ses-activites>). In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026 it [certified 28 correspondents](<https://ipdcp.tg/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-28-correspondants-certifies-par-lipdcp/>), and on 2 and 3 October 2026 it [hosted a delegation from Benin's authority in Lomé](<https://ipdcp.tg/linstance-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-ipdcp-et-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-du-benin-apdp-renforcent-leur-cooperation-a-lome/>). It [signed a cooperation agreement with Mali's authority on 23 September 2026](<https://www.togofirst.com/en/itc/2509-20170-togo-mali-data-regulators-agree-to-share-expertise>). No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

The 2004 organic law [names a national authority for personal data protection, the Instance](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/loi-organique-n-2004-63-du-27-juillet-2004-portant-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>), and [a government decree of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve named members for three years](<https://legislation-securite.tn/ar/latest-laws/%D8%A3%D9%85%D8%B1-%D8%AD%D9%83%D9%88%D9%85%D9%8A-%D8%B9%D8%AF%D8%AF-230-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2021-%D9%85%D8%A4%D8%B1%D8%AE-%D9%81%D9%8A-16-%D8%A3%D9%81%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%84-2021-%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%B9/>). A [bill tabled in July 2025 provides for a new personal data protection authority](<https://www.arp.tn/loi/project/4237>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the Forum Chawki Gaddes [said the authority's activities are at a standstill and called for its reactivation](<https://businessnews.com.tn/2026/10/04/le-forum-chawki-gaddes-denonce-la-divulgation-de-donnees-personnelles-et-appelle-a-proteger-les-mineurs/1421336/>). No renewal of the 2021 appointments, and no ruling or figures, have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

[Section 6 of the Personal Data Protection Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission](<https://www.pdpc.go.tz/media/media/THE_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_ACT.pdf>) as a body corporate, with a seven-member Board and a Director General. On 19 August 2025 it [ruled against an Instagram business page that the report does not name](<https://fbattorneys.co.tz/instagram-photo-triggers-payment-of-fine/>). It also ruled in [Abdul Said Naumanga v. Mi Casa Company Limited](<https://www.rive.co.tz/landmark-ruling-first-pdpc-monetary-award-signals-new-era-for-personal-data-in-tanzania/>). In the last twelve months, Director General Dr Emmanuel Mkilia [announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026](<https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/data-protection-regulator-begins-compliance-crackdown-5574710>). It [certifies data protection officers under a programme launched with the Open University of Tanzania on 14 July 2026](<https://mediawireexpress.co.tz/out-pdpc-launch-national-data-protection-programme/>). No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

Uganda's Personal Data Protection Office, set up under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, [found Google LLC in breach of its registration and transfer duties on 18 July 2025](<https://pdpo.go.ug/media/2025/07/Ssekamwa-Frank-3-Ors-vs-Google-LLC-PDPO-Decision-18th-July-2024.pdf>). On 20 February 2026 it [issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with no fine](<https://businesstimesug.com/whatsapp-updates-privacy-policies-after-uganda-data-protection-enforcement/>). In the last twelve months, on 26 November 2026, it [launched an audit and inspection manual](<https://nilepost.co.ug/news/390990/eight-government-agencies-fail-data-protection-audit>). It also [presented a report on pilot audits of 15 government bodies](<https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/news/eight-government-institutions-fail-data-prote-NV_244898_112026>). No count of its decisions, fines or settled complaints for a period ending in the last two years has been found. Mature would need the Office to publish such a count for a quarter or more.

South Africa's [Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/inforeg-unpacks-regulatory-complexities-posed-by-ai/KA3WwMdzPryvrydZ>) to monitor and enforce POPIA and PAIA. [National Treasury appropriated R135.7m for it for 2025/26](<https://www.treasury.gov.za/documents/National%20Budget/2025May/ene/FullENE.pdf>). It reports [1,355 POPIA complaints in 2024/25, 745 of them resolved](<https://inforegulator.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Information-Regulator-Annual-Report-2025-210mm-x-260mm-1.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [the Polokwane High Court reduced its fine on Blouberg Local Municipality from R500,000 to R250,000 in April 2026](<https://inforegulator.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/INFORMATION-REGULATOR-TURNS-TO-THE-COURTS-TO-FINE-BLOUBERG-LOCAL-MUNICIPALITY-FOR-CONTRAVENTION-OF-POPIA_.pdf>), and in October 2026 it [fined Central Johannesburg TVET College R500,000 and First National Bank R1 million](<https://inforegulator.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/MEDIA-STATEMENT-REGULATOR-FINES-CJC-AND-FNB-FOR-POPIA-CONTRAVENTION.pdf>). [On 11 September 2026 Parliament's Justice Committee invited comment on candidates for vacant positions on it](<https://www.parliament.gov.za/press-releases/media-statement-justice-committee-calls-public-input-candidate-cvs-information-regulator>).

The [Data Protection Commission of Zambia is treated as an existing body in a World Bank tender dated 10 August 2026](<https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/procurement-detail/OP00461498>), which describes it as conducting investigations, issuing determinations and enforcing the law. Its [first Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in June 2023](<https://www.itnewsafrica.com/2025/04/zambias-data-protection-commissioner-fully-operational-enforcing-privacy-compliance/>). In the last twelve months, the [Commissioner, Likando Luywa, spoke on oversight and registration of data controllers in June 2026](<https://lusakastar.com/news/data-protection-act-faces-enforcement-hurdles>). No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

In the last twelve months, in March 2026 it said it had [received 1,123 data controller licence applications that year](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/financial-sector-bears-brunt-of-data-breaches-potraz-calls-for-stronger-data-management/>). It [issued Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 on compliance inspections, which start on 1 September 2026](<https://www.techzim.co.zw/2026/07/potraz-starts-data-protection-inspections-on-1-september-here-is-what-it-means-for-you/>). On 23 October 2026 the ICT minister [directed POTRAZ to investigate unlawful processing of personal information](<https://newshour.co.zw/potraz-ordered-to-crack-down-on-poor-network-service-data-fraud/>).
